checks_run.procedure: My own integration probe of the D-238 open question (D-226, D-228 (1), D-233: 'a token sequence that loses or misplaces a hidden literal after edits, grant changes or concurrent saves'), on the real API. A writer without the grant (ADM_METHOD) edits automation rules whose conditions name a benefit that is later marked sensitive. Every response is scanned for the hidden ids.
checks_run.command: cp qa-r1-token-sequences.test.ts apps/api/test/integration/access/ ($TMPDIR/rv2); QA_PG_PORT=32550-32552 tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --project integration apps/api/test/integration/access/qa-r1-token-sequences.test.ts
checks_run.expected: No sequence loses, misplaces or discloses a hidden literal; refusals name nothing.
checks_run.actual: Run 3: 5/5 pass, exit 0. (1) One token duplicated into two conditions and into an in-list next to the open literal P: the stored conditions are [neq S, in [P,S], neq S]; the response shows tokens at positions 1, 3 and 4, P in clear, and no leak in the rule list, the rule or the version list. (2) The token moved into gt is refused 422 automation_rule.condition_invalid (decimal literals only), nothing is stored, and the body names no id. Moved into eq it stores S. A dry run with benefitId=P answered 201 with outcome fail and conditionsMet false; findings name a field, never a value; nothing in the dry run, the dry-run list or the lists names S. (3) Draft v2 of a published v1, made by the same writer (POST versions with If-Match): v2 issues its own token, a reorder in v2 stores [neq P, neq S], and v1 is unchanged. (4) Two concurrent PATCHes with the same If-Match and tokens: statuses 409/200, the loser's code is version_conflict, and S sits only where the winner put it. (5) A grant between read and save: the token resolves and the response shows S in clear. After revocation, the plain id re-sent with a reorder stores [neq S, neq P], the response shows a token again, and a third save from that token stores [neq P, neq S]. Run 1 failed 2 cases because of errors in my probe (I expected gt to be accepted, and I omitted If-Match on version creation; both are product-correct behaviours); kept as 30-probe-token-sequences.run1-probe-authoring-errors.log. The automation audit events record content_sha256, not conditions, and job runs serve only error codes. Judgement: no defect.

checks_run.procedure: Judge the two open questions of D-238 by reading the code and the served surfaces. D-229: connector configuration names (credential_refs, field_mappings) stay cannot-name. D-228 (4): cross-organization ids are out of scope. Look for a served column, response, notification channel or write path that still names a sensitive record.
checks_run.command: Read apps/api/src/modules/integrations/connectors.ts (config schema, checkFieldMappings), access/sensitive-reach.ts (sensitive types and child sources), automation/versions.ts and dry-run.ts and conditions.ts (summary, presenters, evaluation), jobs/operations.ts (job_run presenter), migrations 0074 and 0104; plus probe QA-RG-R1-10
checks_run.expected: Either a concrete disclosure path (a finding), or a reasoned 'not a defect'.
checks_run.actual:
Not a defect, for either question.
- D-229. Connector configuration names no sensitive record type: the sensitive types are benefit, business case and evidence. The configuration names transformations (targetTransformationId), users (commitOnBehalfOf) and a source system. field_mappings.target is limited to an identifier pattern. The only free text is a mapping source column name and the credential-ref names, set by connector administrators (connector.manage), who also read them (connector.read). A sensitive id typed there by an admin holding the grant would be a deliberate free-text act, like any description field; the product never serializes a record id into these columns.
- Other surfaces checked. The served automation summary is built from the redacted conditions. Action parameters can name only a transformation and roles. Dry-run findings carry field names only. Job runs carry pg-boss job ids and error codes only. The D-227 masked columns are covered by the served-column inventory test, which passes in both integration runs.
- Ordering oracles. gt/gte/lt/lte need decimal literals, so they give no ordering oracle on a hidden uuid. eq/in would need a guess of a 122-bit uuid.
- D-228 (4). Every D-218 helper scopes to the reader's organizations, and no probe route reached another organization's records.
